newsitem.title: USA: California Micro sees slight Q2 profit.
newsitem.headline: California Micro sees slight Q2 profit.

text.p: California Micro Devices Corp on Thursday said it expects to report a slight profit for the second fiscal quarter ended September 30, despite revenue reductions and a significant increase in research and development spending for new products.
In a statement, the company said revenues will be approximately 15 percent below the $9.6 million reported for the quarter ended June 30.
According to First Call, analysts had expected the company to report a profit of $0.05 a share versus $0.08 a year ago.

"This has been a tough quarter for CMD and most of the semiconductor and related industries," California Micro President and Chief Executive Officer Jeffrey Kalb said. "Although orders improved late in the quarter, they were still not as much as we would have liked."

The company said many customers are reducing their inventories and giving the company significantly shorter lead times.In addition the company said it also witnessed a significant reduction in distribution inventories in the quarter.

"As a result, visibility is short and planning is difficult," Kalb added. "Also, some of our customers, in addition to correcting inventory levels, have lost market share in certain key areas, and some customers have delayed production on products where CMD has design wins."
Kalb said the company took steps late in the June quarter and early in the September quarter to significantly reduce costs.
"Recent weeks have shown increased booking levels, but visibility is still very short term," he added.
